title: Kernel Scouting Harness and Golden-window CI Perf Gates for Prefill/Decode Scheduling
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Our CI perf gates and golden baselines detect regressions too late for prefill/decode scheduling changes. Small kernel routing or attention-optimization changes can shift tail latency distributions in ways that are not captured by the current static golden runs. Goal: build a 'kernel scouting' harness that (1) enumerates candidate kernel-routing configurations across a representative cross-cohort workload suite, (2) produces compact golden-window fingerprints (time-of-day + cohort slices) for deterministic CI comparisons, and (3) wires automated perf gates into the CI pipeline that trigger alerts and a canary rollback workflow when drift exceeds thresholds. This ticket implements the harness, integrates it with the workload catalog, and adds CI steps + runbook links for on-call actions.
acceptance_criteria: Kernel scouting harness executes deterministic runs across 10+ cohort slices in <= 4 hours per run on the perf cluster
Golden-window fingerprints generated as stable artifacts (sha + metrics) and stored in S3 with retention policy

CI perf gate step added to runtime-1.25 pipeline: compares current run to golden-window using KS/AD tests and quantile deltas; fails when tail-latency (p99.9) increases > 8% or median token throughput drops > 5%
Playbook and GitHub issue template created that the CI step uses when failing (includes PR checklist for kernel changes)
Documentation: README for running harness locally + Confluence design doc with sampling strategy and statistical model
approach: Create a lightweight 'kernel-scout' runner that accepts a list of kernel routing candidates and a cohort specification; it launches parameterized benchmark jobs and writes metric slices to the golden artifact store
Leverage existing workload corpus but add cross-cohort sampling: short prompt, long-context dialogue, high-embedding density, and prefill-heavy batches to capture prefilling costs
Implement a golden-window fingerprint format: {date-window, cohort-id, seed, kernel-candidate-id, summary-metrics} and a comparator that reports quantile deltas and distributional divergence
Integrate a CI action that pulls the golden artifact, runs a fast synthetic cohort (parallelized), and applies statistical tests (Kolmogorov-Smirnov + trimmed-mean delta) before gating
Add a lightweight canary path: on failure, automatically run a 2x longer canary on dedicated pool and open a templated triage issue with attached traces and kernel telemetry
tradeoffs: Determinism vs. runtime cost: full deterministic golden runs are expensive; we prefer a golden-window (short repeatable runs) plus stochastic canary for coverage
False positives: tightened gates reduce regressions slipping into prod but may slow merges; thresholds chosen to balance alert noise with safety
Storage: persisting full traces for every scaffolded run is costly; store summarized fingerprints and links to traces only for failing canaries
Complexity: adding cohort stratification improves sensitivity but increases test matrix size; initial rollout will cover 6 cohorts and expand if needed
